rows.citation: Srinivasan, M., Kanewala, U. (2022). Metamorphic relation prioritization for effective regression testing. Software Testing, Verification and Reliability, 32(3), e1807.
rows.model_type: general software under test: BBMap read aligner, Weka IBk k-NN classifier, LingPipe bio-entity recognition (not neuron models)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes: first-order mutants from muJava, PIT and Major mutation tools; mutants raising exceptions or not finishing were removed.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: several metamorphic relations, each with source and follow-up inputs, act as a multi-test battery; no physical stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: outputs are alignments, classifications and entity labels; no electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes: greedy fault-based and coverage-based ordering of metamorphic relations, compared with random ordering and an optimal ordering baseline.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: ordering derived on one mutation tool's mutants, evaluated on an independent mutant set from a different tool; no held-out subject programs.
rows.ai_transformations: no: faults are tool-generated code mutants; no AI-assisted edits or translations.
rows.software: none (uses third-party mutation tools muJava, PIT and Major; arXiv preprint https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09798)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic analogue of NeuroSem's selection step (greedy fault-based test ordering, random baseline, independent mutant set). NeuroSem would add neuron-model mutation operators, current-clamp protocols, calibrated eFEL tolerances, cost-matched baselines and held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (type journal-article, issued 2022-02-17, vol 32 issue 3, e1807); Semantic Scholar API (arXiv 2109.09798, DBLP journals/stvr/SrinivasanK22); arXiv PDF full text read (methods, subjects, mutant sets). Preprint dated 2021; journal year 2022 used.
rows.found_via: Crossref: 'metamorphic testing scientific software' [fallback source used because arXiv/OpenAlex were rate-limited]

rows.citation: Stratigopoulos, H.-G., Spyrou, T., Raptis, S. (2023). Testing and Reliability of Spiking Neural Networks: A Review of the State-of-the-Art. 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Defect and Fault Tolerance in VLSI and Nanotechnology Systems (DFT), pp. 1-8.
rows.model_type: neuromorphic spiking-neural-network hardware (mostly integrate-and-fire neurons in digital/analog accelerators)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial: reviews behavioural fault injection (threshold, leak, refractory changes; dead or saturated neurons; weight faults, bit-flips) for hardware, not model-file edits.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: reviewed tests use input image sets, plus one analog-neuron self-test with ramps eliciting several firing patterns.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: one reviewed neuron test checks firing-pattern classes (regular, fast spiking, bursting, chattering); most work measures inference accuracy.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial: reviews compact test-input generation for fault coverage (greedy fault dropping, adversarial examples, confidence-based image ordering).
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: review article; no held-out model or held-out fault-family evaluation of its own.
rows.ai_transformations: no: faults model hardware defects and parameter bit-flips; no AI-assisted code transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Addresses manufacturing and runtime faults in SNN accelerators, scored mainly by task accuracy. NeuroSem targets software edits to biophysical NeuroML/LEMS cell models, eFEL feature tolerances and held-out model evaluation; overlap is compact fault-covering test selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (proceedings-article, IEEE, pp. 1-8, issued 2023-10-03); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs (abstract, DBLP conf/dft/StratigopoulosSR23); author full text on HAL (hal-04176109v1) read.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org differential testing spiking neural network simulators NEST Brian NEURON consistency; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Mulugeta, L., Drach, A., Erdemir, A., et al. (2018). Credibility, Replicability, and Reproducibility in Simulation for Biomedicine and Clinical Applications in Neuroscience. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12, 18.
rows.model_type: mechanistic multiscale neuroscience simulation for clinical use (conceptual verification-and-validation guidance)
rows.controlled_mutations: no: no deliberate fault injection or mutation analysis.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: no stimulation battery; advises checking cell-type firing before building networks.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: recommends verifying proper firing characteristics of cell types, without a defined feature set or tolerances.
rows.protocol_optimization: no: no test or protocol selection method.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: advocates validating against data not used in model development; conceptual guidance, no empirical study.
rows.ai_transformations: no: no AI-assisted model editing or translation discussed.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Frames credibility, V&V and reproducibility, recommending automated test suites at each version update. NeuroSem would operationalise one such regression methodology, reporting finite test evidence as credibility evidence rather than equivalence proof.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (journal-article, Frontiers Media SA, vol 12, article 18, 9 authors); Europe PMC core record (PMID 29713272, PMC5911506); Europe PMC full-text XML scanned (testing and V&V sections).
